html:
The world today faces a significant escalation in the US-Iran conflict, with both sides conducting fresh strikes across the Middle East, threatening to unravel a ceasefire deal and reigniting fears of a broader regional war amidst the funeral observances for Iran's late supreme leader, Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

US-Iran Conflict: Centcom reported hitting 90 Iranian targets, resulting in 14 deaths, while Iran launched retaliatory strikes against American destroyers in the Gulf and infrastructure at US bases in Kuwait, Bahrain, Qatar, and Jordan. Iranian forces also targeted a US command and control center and an American air base in Jordan with ballistic missiles. Saudi Arabia and other Arab states condemned Iran's attacks; Israel stated its readiness for further action, though a Turkish Foreign Minister noted that Iran and the US remain in a ceasefire. The Strait of Hormuz traffic is near a standstill, impacting oil prices. Iran’s new supreme leader is Mojtaba Khamenei, as millions participated in the funeral for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei.

Ukraine War & NATO: Ukraine escalated attacks by striking Russian ships near Crimea, targeting fuel supplies. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy met President Trump at a NATO summit, where Trump said the US would give Ukraine a license to make Patriot air defense systems, pending technical finalization. Russia has banned diesel exports following Ukrainian attacks, straining the global market. At the summit, Turkey's Erdogan gave every NATO leader, including Keir Starmer, a revolver as a parting gift.

UK Political Transition: Outgoing PM Keir Starmer is set to be succeeded by Andy Burnham in just over 10 days, signaling he may award resignation honours. Andy Burnham, the likely next prime minister, made an apology over Gaza, seen as a "reset moment" for Labour to win back progressive voters, following Keir Starmer's previous interview on Israel’s right to defend itself which caused damaging fallout.

Global Economy & Environment: A factory fire in China’s "shoe capital" killed at least 28 people. The US National Weather Service warns of rising risks that a historic El Niño will persist through spring 2027, capable of supercharging extreme weather. This is underscored by France experiencing its third heatwave of the season, and Western Europe recording its hottest June in history.

Regional Security & Crises: In South Africa, anti-migrant protests have intensified, with protesters forcing immigrants from their homes, prompting Doctors Without Borders to warn of growing humanitarian needs. Elsewhere in Africa, the UN is "deeply concerned" by a drone attack in Sudan, an uptick in fighting in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo between the army and M23 militia, and Mali rebels attacking a convoy of Russian and Malian troops.

Gaza & Lebanon: Palestinians mourn aid worker Mohammed al-Wahidi, killed in an Israeli strike, who had organized Gaza World Cup screenings. The ceasefire has left Gaza split, with Israeli forces pushing deeper into the territory. The Palestinian education ministry condemned the demolition of a West Bank primary school by Israeli settlers. US officials state that Lebanon and Israel have entered the next phase of a Hezbollah disarmament deal, with the US guiding an Israeli pullout from "pilot zones."
